description: A simple baseline model that uses plain vision transformers as backbones with lightweight upsampling and heatmap prediction for human pose estimation, demonstrated on MS COCO keypoint estimation.

A simple yet effective vision transformer baseline for human pose estimation that uses plain, non-hierarchical transformer backbones with lightweight decoders and demonstrates scalability and flexibility across model size, input resolution, and pre-training data.

A vision-transformer-based human pose estimation model that uses window-based attention, shift-window and pooling-window strategies, and supports flexible fine-tuning and multi-dataset training; presented with transferability and implementation details for pose estimation.

A simple yet effective vision transformer baseline for human pose estimation that achieves state-of-the-art performance on MS COCO and supports multi-dataset training, partial fine-tuning, and knowledge distillation.

A vision transformer-based human pose estimation model described as a simple baseline, with strong scalability, flexibility, and transferability. It was evaluated primarily on MS COCO and also on AI Challenger, MPII, CrowdPose, and OCHuman; the paper reports 80.9 AP on MS COCO test-dev using a ViTAE-G backbone.
resources.remarks: Mostly aligned with ViTPose as a human pose estimation model/paper; however one description incorrectly describes window-based attention and other details that are not characteristic of ViTPose, so this is not fully perfect.
